Alex — thanks for the time earlier. Per our onboarding plan (DBL-2391) this thread will be the single source for the network & security handoff items so SRE and security can take the next steps. Attached are the initial manifest and a simple VPC config we discussed.

Quick summary / asks for your team before our handoff call: 
- Confirm VPC CIDR ranges you want peered and any overlapping ranges to avoid (we've proposed 10.40.0.0/16 for RBW-hosted subnets).
- Decide whether you prefer BGP (transit) or static route peering for your edge appliance. If BGP, share ASN and peering policy.
- Confirm which private endpoints you need (model inference, metrics ingest, S3-like object access). We will provision endpoint IPs and provide DNS entries in your private zone.
- On-prem package: confirm rack/edge model (appliance SKU) and if HSM/KMS integration is required for key wraps. If yes, provide KMS vendor and support window.
- Firewall & egress: list any outbound egress destinations that must be whitelisted (we usually require outbound to redwood-control.redwood.com:443, package download domains, and telemetry endpoints).

Proposed next step: 30-min technical handoff Tues 2028-03-16 10:00 PT. Please suggest alternate if that doesn't work.

Attachments: cobaltbridge_vpc_config.json, redwood_private_install_manifest.pdf

Thanks,

Sean — thanks, this is helpful. Looping in Priya (networks) and our infra alias. A few quick answers and clarifying Qs: 
- CIDRs: we can accept 10.40.0.0/16 for your side. Our data center uses 10.5.0.0/16 internally; we'll avoid overlap.
- Peering mode: prefer static routes for now; we may move to BGP later. If static, what TTL/keepalive expectations do you have and how do you handle failover between Dedicated and Hosted?
- Private endpoints: we need inference endpoint + metrics ingest. Also want a private S3-compatible endpoint for artifact retrieval. Are DNS suffixes provided as part of the install manifest?
- On-prem appliance: we'll confirm SKU on Friday — likely the rack unit (RBW-200). HSM integration: yes, we use Thales Luna; will need the KMS contact and the cert exchange flow.

The Tue slot works for Priya and Alex (me). Confirm meeting invite and any pre-reads you want us to review.

Priya / Alex — a few technical notes to reduce back-and-forth during the call: 
- Static routes: we will push host routes from our edge into the peering connection. For failover between Dedicated pools and Hosted fallback we use a health-check + route preference; static routes will have lower priority than BGP; we will document the exact route preferences after the call.
- MTU: set peering MTU to 8952 if your appliance supports jumbo frames. If not, 1500 is fine — we recommend 8900+ for better GPU payload performance.
- Keepalives: if you later opt for BGP, we prefer 60s hold / 20s keepalive for stable sessions, but our implementation can accept 30/10 as well.
- DNS: we will publish private DNS entries under cb-internal.redwood.private; we'll coordinate zone delegation if you want them in your resolver.
- Ports: inference endpoints require 443 (TLS) and metrics require 8443 (TLS). Artifact fetch uses 443 to our object-mirror, additional ports only if you request in manifest.

Attached is a lightly annotated diagram of the planned peering and endpoint flows. Please confirm appliance SKU so we can validate VLAN and management IP allocation.

Attachment: network-diagram-v2.png

—Ben
